classification.description: Doors, windows and their frames and thresholds for doors (aluminium)

origin_result.basis: No checks performed; missing a bill of materials and a declaration.

procedure.step: The Ministry of Economy and Tourism registers the factory (prerequisite).
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: The Ministry of Foreign Trade requires the applicant to log in to the e-services portal and choose the Certificate of Origin for India service.
The issuing authority requires the application to include the HS code, description, quantity and value of the exported product, and each item must qualify separately.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade requires the applicant to upload proof of factory registration, the commercial invoice, and, for a trading exporter, the factory's purchase invoice.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade charges a certificate fee of AED 10 to AED 200.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade requires the applicant to submit the application.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade issues the certificate upon approval.
The competent authority issues the certificate before, at, or within 5 working days of export; it is valid for 12 months from issue and covers one import.
The exporter ensures the goods are shipped directly from the UAE to India, or if transit occurs, under customs control with no operations other than unloading, reloading, storage.
The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry and holds origin information under CAROTAR 2020.
The exporter keeps origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least 5 years from the end of the calendar year of issue.

caveats.note: CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
No usable shipment value, so only rates are given.
The CEPA rate reduces BCD and the Agriculture Infrastructure and Development Cess only for lines in Table II. IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS, anti-dumping, safeguard still apply.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
'+' in the rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, which is required before applying for the certificate.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
Fee bands are in AED and apply to the invoice value in AED; no currency conversion is done by Mansha.
The agreement says box 8, but India's origin rules and certificate form say box 9; India's form governs entry into India.
Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system, but this is seen only in secondary sources.
An invoice issued by a third party does not by itself cause the claim to be denied; the exporter must indicate 'third-party invoicing'.

follow_up_questions: Confirm the HS code for aluminium window frames (proposed 76101000).
Provide the shipment value in AED.
Provide a bill of materials with the description, 6-digit HS code, origin country, value and currency of each input.
Provide a declaration with the product price, FOB or Ex-Works basis, final manufacture in the UAE, and operations done in the UAE.
